headline_hook: A Federal Judge Backs Minnesota's AI Ban While Open Models Storm the Frontier
preview_topics: open-weight models crashing the Pareto frontier
a JSON compressor for token-starved prompts

pick_of_the_day.thesis: Minnesota's surviving ban reveals that state-level AI regulation is quietly assembling the patchwork legal framework federal lawmakers can't agree on — and xAI's failed challenge may have actually hardened the precedent it tried to kill.

model_literacy.relevance: Today's open-model roundup ranks Laguna S2.1, Inkling, and Kimi K3 on the Pareto frontier — the curve where no model dominates another on every metric at once. Understanding this concept explains why 'best model' is always the wrong question; the real question is which tradeoffs you're willing to accept for your use case.

items.title: Simon Willison Ships condense-json 1.0 to Squeeze Your Context Windows
items.angle: Every token wasted on JSON formatting is a token you can't spend on reasoning — this tool attacks the problem at the serialization layer
items.key_fact: condense-json 1.0 compresses JSON payloads for LLM consumption, cutting token waste from structural formatting

items.title: Federal Judge Lets Minnesota's AI Nudification Ban Stand Against xAI

items.title: The Habsburg Frog: A Personal Benchmark That Exposes Real Model Differences

items.key_fact: Asking models to draw an SVG frog with a Habsburg jaw produces wildly divergent outputs that map to real capability differences
